Coconino National Forest confirmed today that no fire restrictions are currently in effect forest-wide. No Flood Watch is active for northern Arizona today, but this trail crosses Fossil Creek in a canyon, so avoid hiking during and shortly after any storm. Hike early morning and carry extra water.

south-kaibab-ooh-aah.note: No change since the Park Service expanded closures on September 3, 2026, confirmed unchanged today directly against the NPS news release on the expanded inner canyon closures: South Kaibab Trail is open only from the trailhead to Tip-Off Point (about 4.4 miles down) and closed below that due to hazardous conditions from flash flooding (Source: National Park Service). Ooh Aah Point (0.9 miles) and Cedar Ridge (1.5 miles), the trail's popular shorter destinations, remain within the open section. This follows the severe flash flood in Bright Angel Canyon on August 29 that destroyed nearly all footbridges over Bright Angel Creek; the park states there is no estimated reopening at this time. The NPS continues to warn that additional thunderstorms could bring further flash flooding, debris flows, or rockfall with little to no warning. This trail is fully sun exposed with no water source below the trailhead; confirm current water status at the trailhead before descending. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning is active for Grand Canyon country today; no active NWS alerts were found for the area today (Source: National Weather Service). Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

bright-angel-indian-garden.note: No change since the Park Service expanded closures on September 3, 2026, confirmed unchanged today directly against the NPS news release: Bright Angel Trail remains open only from the trailhead to Havasupai Gardens (formerly Indian Garden) at the Tonto Trail intersection; the trail is closed below that intersection except for river-trip exchanges at Pipe Creek Beach (Source: National Park Service). This follows the severe flash flood in Bright Angel Canyon on August 29 that closed Phantom Ranch, the North Kaibab Trail, and the river-crossing bridges; the park states there is no estimated reopening at this time. Confirm current water status at the trailhead before descending, since prior scheduled shutoffs at the lower resthouses may still be in effect. Grand Canyon National Park separately advises day hikers descend no farther than 1.5 miles from the upper trailhead due to elevated Inner Canyon heat risk regardless of warning status. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning is active for Grand Canyon country today; no active NWS alerts were found for the area today (Source: National Weather Service). Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

rim-trail.note: No closures reported today; the Rim Trail is not affected by the Bright Angel Canyon flash flood closure, confirmed unchanged today. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

north-kaibab-coconino.note: The entirety of North Kaibab Trail, Phantom Ranch (including Bright Angel Campground, the Canteen, and cabins), and the Black Bridge and Silver Bridge river crossings remain closed with no estimated reopening, confirmed unchanged today directly against the NPS news release on the expanded inner canyon closures (Source: National Park Service). The closure follows the severe flash flood that struck Bright Angel Canyon on August 29, destroying nearly all footbridges over Bright Angel Creek and damaging the Transcanyon pipeline that supplies South Rim water. Phantom Ranch reservations remain cancelled and Colorado River traffic through the area remains halted. The National Park Service continues to warn that additional thunderstorms could bring further flash flooding, debris flows, and rockfall with little to no warning. Water status at the North Kaibab Trailhead, Supai Tunnel, and Cottonwood Campground should be considered uncertain until the park posts a post-flood update. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning is active for Grand Canyon country today; no active NWS alerts were found for the area today (Source: National Weather Service). Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.
